newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia ACF to double capital base of finance arm.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia ACF to double capital base of finance arm.

text.p: Malaysia's ACF Holdings Bhd plans to double the capital base of its finance house and open more branches under an expansion plan, company director Michael Chan Heng Lim said on Wednesday.

He told a briefing of analysts that the financial firm plans to raise the capital base of Asia Commercial Finance (M) Bhd to 300 million ringgit from 129.4 million currently. Chan did not give a time frame.
ACF Holdings, a subsidiary of diversified Lion Corp Bhd, expects to be listed on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange this month.
The company is making a public issue of 11.0 million new shares at 2.90 ringgit each, and is offering for sale 35.24 million vendor shares at the same price.
Chan said raising Asia Commercial's capital would hoist the company to a Tier-1 finance house under Malaysian banking rules.

A Tier-1 finance house -- which currently must have minimum shareholders' funds of above 300 million ringgit -- are allowed a more liberal operating environment like remittance services within Malaysia and granting unsecured business loans of up to 500,000 ringgit.

"We plan to obtain a Tier-1 status which allows the company to expand its network further," Chan said. Asia Commercial currently has 56 branches, and Chan did not say how many more branches the company would be opening.
Subsidiaries of ACF Holdings are also in insurance broking, factoring, leasing and hire purchase businesses.
